question.text: Special Situation Fund (SSF) under AIF Regulations is registered as a sub-category under which AIF category, and which Insolvency framework does Chapter 9 specifically mention it can participate in as a Resolution Applicant?

answer.text: Sub-category under Cat III; under the SARFAESI Act only.
Sub-category under Category I AIF; may act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016.
Standalone category; only under RBI's Prudential Framework.
Sub-category under Cat II; under the Companies Act, 2013 only.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 states that under the AIF Regulations, a Special Situation Fund is a sub-category under Category I AIF and must be registered as such. A Special Situation Fund means a Category I AIF that invests in special-situation assets in accordance with its investment objectives and may act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016 — exactly what Option B captures. The Trap: Options A, C and D mis-classify the SSF (as Cat III, standalone, or Cat II) and pair it with the wrong framework (SARFAESI, RBI Prudential Framework, or Companies Act, 2013) instead of the IBC, 2016. Note: The question is testing the source-backed SSF definition: Category I sub-category, resolution applicant under the IBC, 2016. The workbook passage does not describe SEBI enforcement actions for category drift or IBC Board certification requirements for key personnel.
